hms: working tree dirty — CI can't build this, switching locally
building '/nix/store/...-home-manager-generation.drv'...

options.label: Auto-commit, push, then wait on CI
options.description: hms commits everything with a generated message, pushes, waits for the green run, then switches. Matches 'push and wait on ci' literally; every switch becomes a commit.

options.label: Refuse until you commit

questions.question: When the tree IS clean and pushed, should `hms` always wait for CI?

options.label: Only when the local build is expensive
options.description: hms runs nix build --dry-run first. If only the cheap per-commit hm_* config derivations need building (the common case), it switches immediately. It waits on CI only when a real compile is queued.

options.label: Always wait for the green run
options.description: Every switch goes through CI. Predictable and always yields a pure download, but adds ~15 min to even a one-line config tweak.

hms: pushed; waiting on run 63 ...
hms: run 63 success (14m)
Starting home manager activation

options.label: Wait only when asked (hms --ci)
options.description: Default stays exactly as today: a plain local switch. The push-and-wait path is opt-in behind a flag.
options.preview:

$ hms --ci     # push, wait on run, then switch

file.content:
git-credential-fj = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "git-credential-fj" ''
    set -euo pipefail

    # Only `get` is ours to answer — fj owns store/erase.
    [ "''${1:-}" = "get" ] || exit 0

    host=""
    while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
      [ -n "$key" ] || break
      case "$key" in
        host) host="$value" ;;
      esac
    done
    [ -n "$host" ] || exit 0

    keys="''${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/forgejo-cli/keys.json"
    [ -r "$keys" ] || exit 0

    # A nonzero exit aborts git's whole operation rather than falling through
    # to a prompt, so a half-written keys.json degrades to "no credential".
    token=$(${lib.getExe pkgs.jq} -r --arg h "$host" '.hosts[$h].token // empty' "$keys" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
    [ -n "$token" ] || exit 0

    # Forgejo ignores the basic-auth username when the password is a token.
    printf 'username=oauth2\npassword=%s\n' "$token"
  '';

  claude-prof = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "claude-prof" ''
    set -euo pipefail
    CONFIG_HOME="''${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"

  # `hms` — switch this host, but let the forge do the building.
  #
  # A local switch compiles whatever is not in attic; the in-cluster runner has
  # far more of everything and pushes its result to attic, so waiting for CI and
  # then switching turns the switch into a pure download. The wait is only worth
  # it because the closure CI pushes is bit-identical to the one we would build.
  #
  # Refuses on a dirty tree: CI builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch
  # is one CI can never reproduce, and silently building it locally would hide
  # that. `--local` is the escape hatch for exactly that case.
  hms = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "hms" ''
    set -euo pipefail

    repo="$HOME/devel/dotfiles"
    host="$(uname -n)"
    forge="https://forge.ko.ag"
    slug="sauyon/dotfiles"
    curl=${lib.getExe pkgs.curl}
    jq=${lib.getExe pkgs.jq}

    local_only=0
    hm_args=()
    for a in "$@"; do
      case "$a" in
        -l|--local) local_only=1 ;;
        -h|--help)
          echo "usage: hms [--local] [home-manager switch args...]"
          echo "  default: push HEAD, wait for its CI run, then switch (a download)"
          echo "  --local: skip CI and build here"
          exit 0 ;;
        *) hm_args+=("$a") ;;
      esac
    done

    switch_now() {
      exec home-manager switch --flake "$repo#$host" ''${hm_args[@]+"''${hm_args[@]}"}
    }

    # mari (darwin) has no Linux CI job; nix-home.yml builds only these three.
    case "$host" in
      utsuho|setsuna|fujiwara) ;;
      *) echo "hms: $host has no CI job — switching locally" >&2; switch_now ;;
    esac

    [ "$local_only" -eq 0 ] || switch_now

    if [ -n "$(git -C "$repo" status --porcelain)" ]; then
      echo "hms: working tree dirty. Commit before switching:" >&2
      git -C "$repo" status --short >&2
      echo "hms: or run 'hms --local' to build it here." >&2
      exit 1
    fi

    sha=$(git -C "$repo" rev-parse HEAD)
    git -C "$repo" push --quiet origin HEAD:master
    echo "hms: pushed ''${sha:0:7}"

    # The token lands in a 0600 curl config, never in argv or the environment —
    # /proc/<pid>/cmdline and environ are world-readable.
    keys="''${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/forgejo-cli/keys.json"
    tmp=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
    ( umask 077
      printf 'header = "Authorization: token %s"\nsilent\n' \
        "$($jq -r '.hosts["forge.ko.ag"].token' "$keys")" > "$tmp/curlrc" )

    api() { $curl -K "$tmp/curlrc" "$forge$1"; }

    # The workflow's `paths:` filter means a commit touching nothing nix-shaped
    # never starts a run. Give it 90s to appear, then stop waiting for a run that
    # is not coming.
    echo -n "hms: waiting for a run on ''${sha:0:7}"
    run=""; waited=0
    while [ -z "$run" ]; do
      run=$(api "/api/v1/repos/$slug/actions/tasks?limit=20" \
        | $jq -r --arg s "$sha" 'first(.workflow_runs[]
            | select(.head_sha == $s and .workflow_id == "nix-home.yml")
            | .run_number) // empty')
      [ -z "$run" ] || break
      if [ "$waited" -ge 90 ]; then
        echo; echo "hms: no run for ''${sha:0:7} (nothing CI-relevant changed) — switching locally" >&2
        switch_now
      fi
      echo -n "."; sleep 10; waited=$((waited + 10))
    done
    echo; echo "hms: run $run — $forge/$slug/actions/runs/$run"

    status=""
    while :; do
      status=$(api "/api/v1/repos/$slug/actions/tasks?limit=20" \
        | $jq -r --arg n "$run" 'first(.workflow_runs[]
            | select(.run_number == ($n | tonumber)) | .status) // empty')
      case "$status" in
        success|failure|cancelled|skipped) break ;;
      esac
      sleep 15
    done

    if [ "$status" = "success" ]; then
      echo "hms: run $run green — switching (should be a download)"
      switch_now
    fi

    echo "hms: run $run $status" >&2
    # Forgejo 13 exposes no run->job API, but the web job endpoint names the job
    # id in its error body, and /actions/jobs/<id>/logs then serves the log.
    job=$(api "/sauyon/dotfiles/actions/runs/$run/jobs/0" -X POST \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"logCursors":[]}' \
          | ${lib.getExe pkgs.gnugrep} -o 'job_id [0-9]*' | tr -dc '0-9' || true)
    if [ -n "$job" ]; then
      log="$tmp/job.log"
      api "/api/v1/repos/$slug/actions/jobs/$job/logs" > "$log" || true
      echo "--- CI error ---" >&2
      # Timestamps are a fixed 29-char prefix; drop them so the errors read.
      if ! ${lib.getExe pkgs.gnugrep} -aE "^.{29}(error:|warning: error|.*Job failed)" "$log" \
           | cut -c30- | tail -30 >&2; then
        tail -30 "$log" | cut -c30- >&2
      fi
    fi
    echo "hms: not switching. Fix CI, or 'hms --local' to build here." >&2
    exit 1
  '';

  claude-prof = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "claude-prof" ''

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build the Linux home-manager closures and push them to attic, so
# `home-manager switch` on the boxes downloads instead of compiling.
#
# mari (aarch64-darwin) is omitted — an x86_64-linux job can't build darwin.
# Cluster-side details and the traps behind the settings here:
# docs/forgejo-dotfiles-ci.md in the kube repo.
name: nix-home

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths:
      - "flake.nix"
      - "flake.lock"
      - "*.nix"
      - "home/**"
      - "patches/**"
      - ".forgejo/workflows/nix-home.yml"
  # Forgejo has no re-run API; dispatch is the only way to retry.
  workflow_dispatch:

# A closure build is long, and two at once share one dind cgroup.
concurrency:
  group: nix-home-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    # Needs privileged job containers, which only a runner can grant — act
    # ignores `container.options: --privileged`. Do not add it below.
    runs-on: privileged
    # Runs in the nix image itself. It has git and bash but no node, so no
    # `uses:` step can run here, and no awk/sed/grep either.
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      # The `kube` cache public key is public (also in flake.nix); only the
      # token is secret. Pin bounds: >=2.26 parses home.nix, <2.35.1 does not
      # crash mid-build.
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        # In-cluster Service, NOT the public https://attic.ko.ag/kube. Pulling
        # through Cloudflare hairpins out of the cluster and back, and that path
        # cuts any single response at a hard 600s: every run that had to fetch
        # the 2.44 GiB google-fonts NAR died at 601.0s with "HTTP error 200
        # (curl error: Stream error in the HTTP/2 framing layer)", which nix does
        # not retry. Same Service the push step below already uses.
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
        # 32 cores would otherwise start 32 builds inside a 16Gi cgroup.
        max-jobs = 6
        cores = 4
        # The image ships sandbox = false; unsandboxed builds fail here.
        sandbox = true
    steps:
      # Fails in seconds if this landed on an unprivileged runner. Checks the
      # capability, not the sandbox — the sandbox initialises fine without
      # privilege, so it is a false green.
      - name: preflight — job container must be privileged
        run: |
          set -eu
          capeff=
          while IFS=: read -r k v; do
            # /proc/self/status uses a TAB separator.
            if [ "$k" = "CapEff" ]; then capeff="${v//[[:space:]]/}"; fi
          done < /proc/self/status
          echo "CapEff=$capeff"
          if [ "$(( 0x$capeff & (1 << 21) ))" -eq 0 ]; then   # CAP_SYS_ADMIN
            echo "NOT PRIVILEGED — runs-on must be 'privileged'."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "privileged OK; sandbox=$(nix config show sandbox 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"

      # attic is not anonymously readable, and nix silently ignores a substituter
      # it cannot authenticate to — so this must precede any nix command or the
      # job rebuilds everything instead of substituting. Both hosts get an entry:
      # the in-cluster Service is what the substituter above uses, attic.ko.ag is
      # kept so reverting that one line is all it takes to go back through
      # Cloudflare. netrc is matched on host, so the extra line is inert.
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      # Hand-rolled because actions/checkout cannot run in this image. Full
      # clone: a shallow one cannot check out an arbitrary SHA.
      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      - name: build home closures
        run: |
          set -eu
          # --fallback: a substituter that dies mid-NAR otherwise aborts the whole
          # job ("no substituter that can build it") after ten minutes of transfer.
          # With it, an unfetchable path is built locally instead — slower, but the
          # run still ends with a closure to push.
          nix build --fallback --no-link --print-out-paths \
            .#homeConfigurations.utsuho.activationPackage \
            .#homeConfigurations.setsuna.activationPackage \
            .#homeConfigurations.fujiwara.activationPackage \
            | tee /tmp/out-paths

      # The image has no attic-client; run it from a pinned nixpkgs rev.
      # Do NOT echo $ATTIC_TOKEN or enable `set -x` here.
      - name: push closures to attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          ATTIC=github:NixOS/nixpkgs/29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299#attic-client
          nix run "$ATTIC" -- login ko \
            http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN"
          # --jobs 2: the default concurrency OOMKills the server.
          # Unquoted $(cat …) is intended — one argument per out-path.
          # Retried because push is idempotent and a build is expensive.
          ok=
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if nix run "$ATTIC" -- push --jobs 2 ko:kube $(cat /tmp/out-paths); then
              echo "push succeeded on attempt $attempt"
              ok=1
              break
            fi
            echo "push attempt $attempt failed; retrying (already-stored paths dedupe)"
            sleep 20
          done
          [ -n "$ok" ] || { echo "push failed after 3 attempts"; exit 1; }

hms: push, wait for CI, then switch — and print the CI error when it fails

A local switch compiles whatever attic does not have; the in-cluster runner has
far more of everything and pushes its result to attic. Waiting for the run and
then switching turns the switch into a download.

hms is a script now rather than a zsh alias. It refuses on a dirty tree — CI
builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch is one CI can never reproduce,
and quietly building it locally would hide that. `hms --local` is the old
behaviour, and is also the fallback when the host has no CI job (mari) or when
the commit touched nothing the workflow's `paths:` filter matches.

On a red run it prints the job's error lines rather than just a status, e.g.

  error: unable to download '.../nar/<hash>.nar': HTTP error 200 ...
  error: path '...-google-fonts-...' is required, but there is no substituter

Forgejo 13 has no run->job API; the web job endpoint names the job id in its
error body and /actions/jobs/<id>/logs then serves the log. The forge token is
read from keys.json into a 0600 curl config, never argv or the environment.

concurrency now queues instead of cancelling. The group still serializes, so two
builds never share the dind cgroup, but a follow-up push no longer discards the
run hms is blocked on — that killed runs 58, 59 and 60.

## 1. `hms` now pushes, waits on CI, then switches

A script in `home.nix` (was a one-line zsh alias). Verified against the live forge:

| Path | Verified |
|---|---|
| `--help` | prints usage, exits 0 |
| Dirty tree | refuses, lists the files, points at `--local`, exit 1 |
| Find run for a SHA | jq returns `62` for run 62's SHA; empty for an unknown SHA |
| Poll status | returns `success` for run 62 |
| **Failure output** | ran it against run 61's real log — printed the 4 `error:` lines + `Job failed` |
| `bash -n` + shellcheck | clean (2 SC2016 infos, both false positives on jq's `$s`/`$n`) |

Fallbacks so it never traps you: `--local` skips CI entirely; a host with no CI job (mari) switches locally; a commit that matches nothing in the workflow's `paths:` filter waits 90 s, says so, and switches locally.

Token handling follows your rule — read from `keys.json` into a `0600` curl config under a `mktemp -d`, never argv or environment.

## 2. `cancel-in-progress: false`

Queues instead of cancelling. The group still serializes, so two builds never share the dind cgroup — but a follow-up push no longer discards the run `hms` is blocked on. This was load-bearing for #1, not optional.

29 families, 121 files. Built it and listed the output rather than trusting a green build — a name matching no file is dropped silently. All 29 present; `PTSans` was the one candidate that matched nothing, so it's out.

**Loop closed. `hms` at HEAD is now a 6.4 MiB download — zero derivations to build.**

That's the whole point of the exercise, and it's the first time it's been true:

```

```

No `will be built` line at all. Before today the same command planned 16+ derivations on top of gigabytes of fetching, and CI — which is what puts those paths in attic — had failed 47 of its first 61 runs.

Run 64 verified from its log: zero `error:` lines, google-fonts built at the new trimmed hash, `push succeeded on attempt 1`, `Job succeeded`.

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| CI success rate | 2 / 61 | 3 green in a row (62, 63, 64) |
| google-fonts NAR | 2.44 GiB | 61 MiB |
| Local `hms` plan | 16 derivations + GiB of fetch | 0 built, 6.4 MiB |

Four commits, each reviewed clean on four angles: `f45a5e3` (nix-home attic path), `a074f96` (vulnix-scan, same bug), `47f184f` (hms + concurrency + fonts).

content.text: Root cause: `hms` pushes unconditionally with no fetch and no ahead/behind check. Local is 1 commit *behind* origin (another machine pushed), so `git push HEAD:master` is correctly rejected — and `set -e` kills the script, dumping raw git hints instead of guidance. It would also have waited on a run for a SHA that isn't what `origin/master` holds.

input.old_string:
sha=$(git -C "$repo" rev-parse HEAD)
    git -C "$repo" push --quiet origin HEAD:master
    echo "hms: pushed ''${sha:0:7}"
input.new_string:
# Fetch before deciding: these boxes push to each other constantly, so an
    # unconditional `push HEAD:master` loses the race regularly, and `set -e`
    # would turn that into a wall of git hints. Worse, waiting on a run for a SHA
    # that is not what origin/master holds would be waiting on the wrong build.
    # Rebasing is a history decision, so say what is wrong and stop.
    git -C "$repo" fetch --quiet origin master
    sha=$(git -C "$repo" rev-parse HEAD)
    remote=$(git -C "$repo" rev-parse origin/master)
    if [ "$sha" = "$remote" ]; then
      echo "hms: ''${sha:0:7} is already origin/master"
    elif git -C "$repo" merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote" "$sha"; then
      git -C "$repo" push --quiet origin HEAD:master
      echo "hms: pushed ''${sha:0:7}"
    else
      behind=$(git -C "$repo" rev-list --count "$sha..$remote")
      ahead=$(git -C "$repo" rev-list --count "$remote..$sha")
      echo "hms: origin/master (''${remote:0:7}) has $behind commit(s) you do not have." >&2
      if [ "$ahead" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "hms: and you have $ahead it does not — rebase, then re-run." >&2
      else
        echo "hms: you are strictly behind — pull, then re-run." >&2
      fi
      git -C "$repo" --no-pager log --oneline "$sha..$remote" | head -5 >&2
      exit 1
    fi

One-shot tuning for the btrfs-on-LUKS-on-loop-on-ext4 home stack: sets LUKS

Secrets are decrypted using `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` as an age identity. On a new machine, either copy your existing key or generate one and add it as a sops recipient:

```bash
# Add new machine key as recipient
cd ~/devel/dotfiles
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
mise run sops -- updatekeys secrets.yaml
```

## Applying changes: `hms`

`hms` is the normal way to switch. It does **not** build locally by default — it
pushes, waits for the commit's CI run, then switches, which turns the switch into
a download of the closure the runner already built and pushed to attic.

```bash
hms              # push, wait for the run, then switch
hms --local      # skip CI and build here (the old `home-manager switch` alias)
```

Things it deliberately refuses rather than works around:

- **A dirty tree.** CI builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch is one CI
  can never reproduce. Commit, or use `--local`.
- **A stale checkout.** If `origin/master` has commits you do not, it says so and
  stops — rebasing is your call, and waiting on a run for a SHA that is not
  `origin/master` would be waiting on the wrong build.

It falls back to a local build, with a note, when the host has no CI job (mari)
or when the commit touched nothing `nix-home.yml`'s `paths:` filter matches. On a
red run it prints the job's actual `error:` lines, not just a status.

Why this is worth a wait: see `docs/ci-nix-home.md`. The short version is that
the runner has far more of everything than these boxes, and its output is
bit-identical to what a local build would produce.

## Commit and Push Policy

This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation. The global "ask before public communications" rule does not apply here.

## Applying config: use `hms`, not `home-manager switch`

`hms` (defined in `home.nix`, documented in `README.md`) pushes, waits for the
commit's CI run on `forge.ko.ag`, then switches — so the switch is a download of
the closure the in-cluster runner built, not a local compile. Expect it to block
for ten-odd minutes. `hms --local` builds here instead.

It refuses on a dirty tree and on a checkout behind `origin/master`. **Both
refusals are the feature.** CI can only build a pushed commit, so do not route
around them with a bare `home-manager switch` — commit and push, or pass
`--local` deliberately and say that you did.

If a run goes red, `hms` prints the job's `error:` lines; read those rather than
re-running blind. Background on why CI is worth waiting for — and the 600s attic
transfer ceiling that made it unreliable for its first 61 runs — is in
`docs/ci-nix-home.md`.

input.new_string:
elif git -C "$repo" merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote" "$sha"; then
      # Fetching narrows the race but cannot close it — another box can advance
      # origin/master between the fetch and the push. Catch that rather than let
      # `set -e` surface the same hint wall this block exists to avoid.
      if git -C "$repo" push --quiet origin HEAD:master 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "hms: pushed ''${sha:0:7}"
      else
        echo "hms: push lost the race — origin/master moved just now. Re-run." >&2
        exit 1
      fi
